audit.why: 44.95% over 732 games with the chart Tryndamere at every single row supports HARD 8/10 and an 8.5/10 carry threat.
All seven rows read Tryndamere in packet.levelChart, win[] and phases[].side alike — no disagreement between layers, and no row where a genuine flip could be evidenced.
audit.corrected: No chart edits. Undying Rage's 120/100/80s added to spikes[1] — it matches Purgatory rank for rank, which is the real reason the level-6 row does not flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two invented mechanics: that Locke's W self-damage feeds Tryndamere's Fury, and that Spinning Slash 'refreshes on kills'. Mocking Shout is absent from the page entirely.
audit.why: Fury is gained from Tryndamere's own attacks, critical strikes and killing blows — damage Locke deals to himself has nothing to do with it. Riot's text for Spinning Slash is a 650-range slice toward a target unit on 12/11/10/9/8s, with no refresh clause. Mocking Shout (14s, 850 range) reduces surrounding champions' Attack Damage and slows enemies whose backs are turned — which is exactly Locke disengaging after a bite, and it never appeared. Bloodlust also raises his AD the more wounded he is, so chipping him without killing him arms him.
audit.corrected: The Fury-from-your-self-damage claim removed; the E refresh claim replaced with Mocking Shout's backs-turned slow; Bloodlust's wounded-AD scaling stated in early.

edits.before: Tryndamere is winning already: his Spinning Slash (E) gap-closes onto you and his crit-fueled autos plus Bloodlust (Q) heal shred you faster than your Q nails and W burst can answer, and your W self-damage only speeds his Fury build.
edits.after: Tryndamere is winning already: his Spinning Slash (E) gap-closes onto you and his crit-fuelled autos plus the Bloodlust (Q) heal shred you faster than your Q nails and W burst can answer, and Mocking Shout slows you the moment you turn to leave.

edits.before: Undying Rage (R) is the wall your entire kit crashes into: Purgatory (R) is an execute totem, but he cannot die under 5 seconds of guaranteed survival, so your ult is dead value the moment he flips it.
edits.after: Undying Rage (R) is the wall your kit crashes into, and at 120/100/80 seconds it matches Purgatory rank for rank: he cannot die while it holds, so your ult is dead value the moment he flips it.

edits.before: This is a losing lane from level 1. Tryndamere's autos and Bloodlust heal outpace your Q-nail poke, and every time your W self-damage chunks you he converts it into Fury for a bigger spin crit. Do not try to win short trades; farm at max range, use E purely defensively to disengage his Spinning Slash, and give up the lane rather than the kill.
edits.after: This is a losing lane from level 1. Tryndamere's autos and Bloodlust heal outpace your Q-nail poke, and Bloodlust hands him MORE attack damage the lower he drops, so chip that does not kill him arms him. Do not try to win short trades; farm at max range, use E purely defensively against Spinning Slash, and give up the lane rather than the kill.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 he only gets scarier as Fury crits ramp. The core problem is level 6: Undying Rage makes him unkillable for its duration, which is a hard counter to your execute-totem identity. Never blow Purgatory while his R is up or available. Farm, ping for jungle pressure, and treat every all-in he starts as something you survive rather than win.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 he only gets scarier as Fury crits ramp, and Mocking Shout (W) slows you whenever your back is turned, so walking out of a trade costs more than it looks. The core problem is 6: Undying Rage makes him unkillable for its duration, a hard counter to your execute identity. Never blow Purgatory while his R is available; farm and ping for jungle pressure.

edits.before: Stack Fury off your W self-damage trades, then all-in with Spinning Slash (E)
edits.after: Stack Fury off attacks and crits, then all-in with Spinning Slash (E)

edits.before: Chase resets with E through minions since it refreshes on kills
edits.after: Cut off your retreat with Mocking Shout's backs-turned slow

notes: Two fabricated mechanics removed. Locke's W self-damage does not build Tryndamere's Fury — Fury comes from his own attacks, crits and killing blows — and Riot's text gives Spinning Slash no kill refresh, so I replaced that line rather than restate an unverifiable one. The genuinely missing ability is Mocking Shout: it cuts your AD and slows you specifically when your back is turned, which is precisely the moment a Locke tries to leave after a bite. Bloodlust also scales his AD with how wounded he is, so poking him without killing him makes his counter-swing bigger.
